svg.title: What happens to a contact form submission, from the click to the CRM
svg.desc: A left-to-right sequence for one lead. The form posts JSON to the lead route. The route rejects unparseable bodies, then rejects a body that fails the schema. It reads the client address from the first hop of the forwarded-for header. A filled honeypot field is accepted with a success status and nothing is stored, so a bot learns nothing from the response. Turnstile is asked whether the submitter is human and a failure is rejected. The business identity is read from site settings, because the consent text has to name the specific business. The capture step checks the suppression list first, then opens one transaction: the lead row is inserted with the consent text regenerated on the server, the disclosure version, a hashed address and a retention date ten years out. Only if the person is not suppressed is an outbox row inserted in that same transaction. Email is best effort and its failures are swallowed, because the lead is already committed. The visitor gets a created response either way. Delivery happens later: a host timer posts to the job route once a minute, which claims due rows and sends them to the CRM.
